newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak state telecom sees SKK 4.4bln 1996 gross.
newsitem.headline: Slovak state telecom sees SKK 4.4bln 1996 gross.

text.p: Slovakia's state-owned fixed line telephone monopoly, Slovenske Telekomunikacie s.p. (ST), said on Monday it expected to post a 1996 gross profit of 4.4 billion crowns ($135.8 million), more than double the previous year.
ST Director Peter Valent said the preliminary result, achieved on income of about 11 billion crowns, was 600 million crowns higher than original plans for last year.
"A major part of last year's profit will be used to cover our investment projects, which are estimated at 8.4 billion in 1997," Valent told a news conference.
ST plans to increase the number of fixed-line telephone stations to 1.38 million in 1997, from some 1.24 million in operation at the end of last year.

Earlier this month, ST signed a $170 million, five-year syndicated loan arranged by Citibank International and ING Barings, to help finance its ambitious modernisation project expected to total 48.7 billion crowns over the next four years.
According to credit conditions for state companies, loans can only only cover 40 percent of the firm's investment plans.
"By the year 2000, we should fully digitalise our telephone network compared with the current digitalisation of 38 percent, which will bring us to EU standards," Valent said.

At present, the density of ST's network is 23 percent and the company plans to increase this to 25.5 percent by the end of this year. The density should meet the EU standard of 35 percent by the year 2000.

ST Financial Director Maria Rokusova said the company and finance ministry would present a plan for the so-called "price mechanism" by the end of May, a measure which would allow ST to fully include its costs in prices of provided services.
"This move is one of the conditions for the future entry of foreign investor to ST," Rokusova said.
Prices of basic telephone services are still regulated by the state, and the finance ministry last allowed ST to increase prices in July 1995.
Valent said preparation of ST's transformation to a 100- percent state-held joint-stock company has been completed and that the firm is awaiting a government decision on the move.

Transformation of ST, one of the few fully state-owned phone companies in the region, is the first step to future partial privatisation, planned through the entry of a foreign strategic partner in 1998. ($ = 32.40 Slovak Crowns)
